To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the “reproducilibity crisis” affects microbiology as well as other disciplines, (2) reproducibility is a complex and multifaceted problem, (3) there are many reasons why researchers cannot reproduce a result, and (4) the best way to improve the reproducibility of research is to make the research process more transparent and to encourage researchers to openly discuss and learn from failures to reproduce results.

(a) microbiome research has been subject to reproducibility crises in the past and will be subject to reproducibly crises in the future, and (b) microbiome researchers can and must do more to ensure that our methods, results, and conclusions are reproducible, replicable, robust, and generalizable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reproducible science of microbiomes.
the reproducibility of microbiome research, but we should not be concerned about the reproducibility crisis in microbiome research.

the reproducibility of microbiome research, and this Perspective outlines a framework to help microbiologists identify and overcome threats to reproduciblity, replicability, generalizability, and robustness of their own work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microbiome research is reproducible, but the reproducibility of microbiome research is not perfect.
the microbiome is reproducible and that microbiome research can be reproducible.
the microbiome field has a reproducibility problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
“reproducible research” is not a single goal but a collection of goals, and the pursuit of these goals requires a variety of methods and strategies.
the reproducibility crisis is a crisis in reproducibility.
we are trying to identify and overcome barriers to reproducibility in microbiome research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reproducibility, and its close relatives, is not a binary property of a study but is a continuum of properties that can be improved.
the microbiome research community should be more open to sharing data, code, and protocols, and that we should be willing to engage in more critical discussions of the work of others.
we need to be more explicit about the assumptions that are built into our methods, and we should be open to the fact that our results are contingent on those assumptions.
